question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of human papillomavirus is the main cause of cervical dysplasia and cancer. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h1)

question: A 55-year-old woman after menopause visits the clinic reporting unexpected vaginal bleeding for two weeks. What condition must be urgently investigated first?
explanation: Any bleeding after menopause is a red flag that requires immediate investigation to rule out malignancy of the cervix or endometrium. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which procedure provides the definitive tissue confirmation for cervical cancer?
explanation: A tissue biopsy taken during examination allows pathologists to view malignant cells under a microscope for a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is the FIGO staging system for cervical cancer primarily based on clinical examination rather than advanced imaging?

options.A: Because imaging tools are proven to be entirely inaccurate
options.B: To match the staging rules used exclusively for breast cancer
options.C: To keep staging accessible in settings where advanced imaging is scarce
options.D: Because clinical exams are completely painless for every patient

explanation: Clinical staging allows providers in low-resource environments to accurately grade and plan care for patients without relying on costly MRI or CT scanners. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h2)

question: At which stage is radical surgery most commonly offered as a primary treatment for cervical cancer?

options.A: Advanced Stage III with kidney failure
options.B: Early stages (Stage I to early Stage IIA)

explanation: Surgery works best when the tumor is small and confined locally to the cervix and upper vagina without spreading to the pelvic wall. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h3)

question: A young woman who has never given birth is diagnosed with microinvasive cervical cancer (Stage IA1). What surgical approach is best suited if she wants to bear children later?
explanation: Conization removes the diseased portion of the cervix while leaving the main body of the uterus intact, preserving potential future fertility. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer from stage IIB to IVA?
explanation: Advanced tumors that have spread beyond the cervix respond much better to a combination of radiation and chemotherapy than to surgery. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is brachytherapy often used after external beam radiation in cervical cancer management?

options.A: To stimulate rapid regeneration of normal cervical tissue
options.B: To completely replace the need for any diagnostic biopsy
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing hair loss
options.D: To deliver a very high dose of radiation directly to the tumor while protecting nearby healthy organs

explanation: Brachytherapy places the radiation source right at the tumor site, maximizing local cancer cell destruction without over-exposing the bladder and bowel. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in patients with advanced metastatic cervical cancer?

options.D: Maximizing comfort and quality of life

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving distressing physical and psychological symptoms when curative treatment is no longer possible. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which framework guides the management of chronic cancer pain in palliative settings?
explanation: The World Health Organization analgesic ladder provides a step-by-step approach to prescribing pain relievers based on pain severity. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main objective of giving the HPV vaccine to young adolescent girls?

options.A: Immediate treatment for active pelvic infections
options.C: Primary prevention against high-risk viral strains

explanation: Vaccines prevent initial infection with high-risk HPV types, thereby stopping the cancerous process before it begins. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of secondary prevention for cervical cancer?

options.B: Administering chemotherapy to a patient with Stage IV disease
options.C: Screening women with a Pap smear
options.D: Performing Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)

explanation: Giving chemotherapy to treat advanced disease is a form of treatment, whereas screening and early detection tests represent secondary prevention. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h6)
